items.description: Report managed-destination replacement failures as CLI errors.
evidence: src/specle/inventory.py:255-260 performs replacements outside the staging error handler.
src/specle/inventory.py:290-299 can raise OSError from rmtree(), unlink(), or replace().
src/specle/main.py:56 catches only SkillInstallationError and SkillMetadataError.
items.analysis: A permission, deletion, or rename failure after staging is currently emitted as an unhandled traceback. This diverges from the design's replacement-failure contract, which requires an actionable report naming the destination and keeping the index unchanged unless its own replacement succeeded.
items.recommendation: Wrap each managed replacement in an error translation that names its destination, retains the staged-file cleanup where possible, and add a regression test for a replacement failure before index replacement.
items.decision_rationale: The replacement-failure contract is required for safe forced installation and has been implemented by the completed bounded bugfix.

dispatch.reason: The completed sidecar bugfix provides the destination-specific error translation, transactional resource preservation, and regression coverage requested by this finding.

items.description: Reject managed destination paths that escape the selected target through symlinks.
items.analysis: A symlinked .agents or managed parent can direct initialisation writes outside the requested target.
items.recommendation: Reject symlinked managed path components before staging or replacement.
items.decision_rationale: Managed symlinks may deliberately direct the shared installation elsewhere; rejecting them would prevent an intended user configuration.

items.description: Prevent concurrent initialisations from bypassing collision preflight.
items.analysis: Concurrent writers can both pass the non-force preflight and interleave replacements.
items.recommendation: Serialise initialisation or recheck destinations immediately before replacement.
items.decision_rationale: Concurrent initialisation is outside the lightweight installer contract and does not justify locking or serialisation complexity.

items.description: Remove newly installed managed destinations when forced initialisation rolls back.
items.analysis: Rollback restores only backed-up destinations, leaving newly created files that block a later non-force retry.
items.recommendation: Track new destinations installed during an attempt and remove them before restoring backups.
items.decision_rationale: A failed initialisation must not leave managed files that obstruct a safe retry.

dispatch.reason: The initialisation contract, design, and task plan now require rollback to remove newly created managed destinations before restoring backups.

items.description: Avoid a transient missing installed index during forced replacement.
items.analysis: Replacing the specle skill directory briefly removes its nested index before the final index write.
items.recommendation: Decide whether uninterrupted index availability is required and, if so, redesign replacement around that contract.
items.decision_rationale: Uninterrupted index availability during a forced local replacement is outside the lightweight installer scope.

items.description: Treat dangling managed symlinks as existing destinations.
items.analysis: Path.exists() misses a dangling symlink, allowing non-force replacement without preserving the link.
items.recommendation: Use lexists-equivalent handling or reject managed symlinks under the target-boundary policy.
items.decision_rationale: Dangling managed symlinks are part of the same deliberate user-controlled path policy and do not require special handling.

items.description: Clean partially created staging paths after copy failures.
items.analysis: Temporary paths are registered only after copying succeeds, so a failed copy can leave partial staging content.
items.recommendation: Register each temporary path before copying and clean it after a staging failure.
items.decision_rationale: Best-effort cleanup of a failed local staging copy is sufficient for the lightweight installer.

items.description: Reject packaged skill directories that lack SKILL.md.
items.analysis: Glob-based discovery can omit an incomplete skill directory while continuing with other valid skills.
items.recommendation: Enumerate skill directories and fail when any lacks its required entrypoint.
items.decision_rationale: The packaged source inventory is controlled by Specle; orphan directories are not supported installer input.

items.description: Translate unreadable packaged metadata into a CLI packaging error.
items.analysis: An OSError or decode error reading SKILL.md bypasses the CLI's handled metadata errors.
items.recommendation: Wrap metadata read and decode failures in SkillMetadataError with the source path.
items.decision_rationale: Unreadable package resources indicate a broken local installation and do not require an additional CLI-specific recovery path.

items.analysis: The comment itself records that the current branch already updated the README and installed-index description.
items.recommendation: Decline as already addressed in the reviewed branch.
items.decision_rationale: The source comment confirms that the current branch already updated the affected documentation.

items.description: Do not resolve index resource paths through pre-existing symlinks.
items.analysis: Resolving an intended installed path before replacing a symlink can embed the old target in index.json.
items.recommendation: Generate file URIs from the lexical intended target path or resolve this with the symlink-boundary policy.
items.decision_rationale: Resource identifiers may intentionally follow a user-configured symlink target.

items.description: Report retained backups that cannot be cleaned after a successful replacement.
items.analysis: Successful replacement suppresses backup-cleanup errors, leaving hidden retained trees without notice.
items.recommendation: Report retained backup paths or define an explicit recovery policy.
items.decision_rationale: Retained backup cleanup residue is recoverable and does not warrant changing the successful-install protocol.

items.description: Recover from process interruption after moving a destination to backup.
items.analysis: A process stop between backup and replacement bypasses in-process rollback and can strand the backup.
items.recommendation: Define persistent transaction recovery if crash resilience is part of the installer contract.
items.decision_rationale: Persistent recovery after abrupt process termination is outside the current lightweight installer contract.

items.description: Test missing usage independently of missing description.
items.analysis: The existing fixture omits both fields, so it cannot prove usage validation independently.
items.recommendation: Add a valid-description, missing-usage test case.
items.decision_rationale: The combined missing-metadata case is sufficient coverage for the constrained frontmatter parser.
